Subject: Draft: Audit export formats, retention proof, and delivery options

Summary (short): Redwood provides tenant-scoped platform audit logs (auth events, console/admin changes, API request metadata, routing/fallback events) and separate inference-level traces (call inputs/outputs) that are only exported on request under customer data agreements. For standard evidence handbacks we recommend exporting the platform audit logs only.

1) Streams included by default in a "platform audit export":
- authentication events (login success/failure, token creations)
- authorization policy evaluations (role changes, permission grants)
- console/admin activity (user creation, role assignments, config changes)
- API request metadata (request id, timestamp, client ip, model version, latency)
- routing and fallback events (when requests were routed to a fallback model/region)

Filters: Exports can be scoped by time-range, event-type (above categories), and by tenant id. We also support event-level selectors to exclude IP addresses or redact request metadata fields if required under DPIA constraints.

2) Delivery & Formats:
- Delivery: S3 push to customer-owned bucket in the requested region (preferred), or time-limited signed HTTPS download. S3 delivery uses per-archive KMS envelope encryption with the customer's KMS key if provided; otherwise Redwood-managed KMS is used and we include key metadata in the manifest.
- Formats: newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) and partitioned Parquet (snappy) for larger exports. Archives are provided as gzipped tarballs (tar.gz) with one file per day/stream partition.
- Hashing: We provide SHA-256 hash for each archive and an overall manifest-level digest. Hashes are included in the manifest and signed by Redwood's export service using an internal signing key; for legal-chain purposes we can provide the public key fingerprint and signing metadata.

3) Retention & deletion proof:
- TTL model: Audit logs are governed by tenant retention policy (configurable 30 days — 7 years). For deletion proof we can provide an export audit that shows deletion jobs ran, timestamps, affected partitions, and tombstone markers.
- Attestation: We offer a signed attestation document that summarizes retention windows and confirms that older partitions were removed at the configured TTL. This attestation includes export job ids, execution timestamps, and the SHA-256 digest of the exported subset used for the attestation.

4) Scope notes on inference-level traces:
- Inference-level traces contain customer payloads and are treated as customer data. We only export those on explicit written request, with redaction options and additional approvals. If Acme needs model I/O for a regulatory investigation, we'll need an escalation and a scoped data-sharing agreement (we can include that language).

Recommended manifest fields (we include a machine-readable sample manifest with our exports):
- export_id, tenant_id, stream_type, start_ts, end_ts, file_name, file_sha256, file_size_bytes, kms_key_id, signed_by, signing_key_fingerprint
